body: Which tag creates the largest heading by default?
explanation: <h1> is the top-level heading. <head> holds page metadata and <header> is a page section, not a heading.

body: Which attribute of the <a> tag holds the link address?
explanation: href (hypertext reference) holds the URL the link points to. src is used by images and scripts.

body: Which tag displays an image?
explanation: embeds an image. The other tags do not exist in HTML.

body: Which CSS property changes the colour of text?
explanation: The property is simply color. font-color and text-color are not valid CSS.

body: Which element creates a numbered list?
explanation: <ol> is an ordered (numbered) list. <ul> is bulleted; <li> is a single item inside either.

body: How do you select the element with id="menu" in CSS?
explanation: # selects by id, . selects by class, and a bare name selects by tag.

body: What does CSS stand for?
explanation: Cascading refers to how rules from many sources combine and override each other.

body: Which input type hides the characters as the user types?
explanation: type="password" masks the typed characters. type="hidden" is not shown on the page at all.

body: Which element is meant to wrap the main navigation links of a site?
explanation: <nav> is the semantic element for major navigation blocks and helps screen-reader users find them.

body: Which property adds space between an element's content and its border?
explanation: padding is inside the border; margin is outside it.

body:
With the default box-sizing, how wide is this box on screen?

.box { width: 200px; padding: 10px; border: 2px solid; }
explanation: With content-box sizing, width covers only the content: 200 + 10 + 10 (padding) + 2 + 2 (border) = 224px.

body:
How wide is this box on screen?

.box { box-sizing: border-box; width: 200px; padding: 10px; border: 2px solid; }
explanation: With border-box, the width already includes padding and border, so the box stays 200px.

body: Which selector has the highest specificity?
explanation: An id selector outweighs any number of class and tag selectors.

body: Which display value lets you use justify-content and align-items to arrange children in a row?
explanation: display: flex turns the element into a flex container; its children are laid out in a row by default.

body: In a flex container with the default row direction, which property centres items horizontally?
explanation: justify-content works along the main axis, which is horizontal for a row. align-items works on the cross axis.

body: Which CSS unit is relative to the root (<html>) font size?
explanation: rem = root em. em is relative to the current element's font size, which can compound when nested.

body: Which attribute makes a form field mandatory before the form can be submitted?
explanation: Adding required makes the browser block submission until the field is filled.

body: What is the alt attribute on an for?
options: Text read by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load
Adding a caption below the image
Linking the image to another page
explanation: alt text describes the image for people using screen readers and appears when the image cannot load.

body: Which media query applies styles only on screens 600px wide or narrower?
explanation: max-width: 600px matches viewports up to and including 600px. min-width matches 600px and wider.

body: An element with position: absolute is positioned relative to what?
options: Its nearest ancestor whose position is not static
explanation: Absolute positioning uses the closest positioned ancestor. Only if there is none does it fall back to the initial containing block.

body: Which element is the best semantic choice for a self-contained blog post?
explanation: <article> marks content that makes sense on its own, such as a post or news story.
When two rules have the same specificity, the one that appears later wins.
!important beats normal declarations, including inline styles that are not marked !important.

body: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
options: display: none keeps the space; visibility: hidden removes it
display: none removes the element's space; visibility: hidden keeps its space
explanation: A visibility: hidden element is invisible but still takes up room in the layout; display: none takes it out of the layout.

body: A 600px-wide grid has grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr; and no gap. How wide are the columns?
explanation: fr units share the free space in proportion: 3 parts in total, so 1 part = 200px and 2 parts = 400px.

body: Two block elements are stacked. The first has margin-bottom: 20px and the second has margin-top: 30px. How much space is between them?
explanation: Vertical margins between blocks collapse: the larger margin is used instead of the sum.

body: Which <meta> tag is needed so a responsive layout displays correctly on phones?
explanation: Without the viewport tag, mobile browsers render the page as a wide desktop page and shrink it down.

body: What is the difference between the selectors ul > li and ul li?
options: ul li matches only direct children
ul > li matches only direct children; ul li matches li at any depth inside ul
ul > li matches the next sibling of ul
explanation: > is the child combinator. A space is the descendant combinator, which matches nested items too.

body: Why is <button> better than a <div> with an onclick handler for a clickable control?
options: A div cannot have a click handler
A button can be reached with the keyboard and is announced as a button by screen readers
explanation: Native buttons come with keyboard focus, Enter/Space activation and the correct role. A div needs all of that added by hand.

body: You set z-index: 10 on an element but it still appears behind others. What is the most likely cause?
options: The element has a background colour
10 is too small to have an effect
explanation: z-index only applies to positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) and flex/grid items. Static elements ignore it.
